pattern_title: Authorization code distribution changes are a gating issue before action
pattern_description: A large share of the increase is tied to authorization code distribution changes rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement signal. CA is the largest exposure, with the same issue also appearing in AR and IN. This should be treated as a front-end validation problem before any medical management or provider action is taken.

rows.policy_relevance: United Health reimburses hepatic fibrosis testing every 180 days; multianalyte assay codes not separately reimbursable.

individual_policies.policy_title: Hepatic Fibrosis Testing for Chronic Liver Disease Policy, Professional and Facility - Reimbursement Policy - UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange
individual_policies.evidence: Reimbursable for specified liver disease conditions once every 180 days; no prior authorization stated.

individual_policies.policy_title: MEDADV Hepatic Fibrosis Testing Chronic Liver Disease Policy
individual_policies.evidence: This policy does not address DRG payment or authorization code distribution changes. The relevant overlapping rule is that this hepatic fibrosis test is separately reimbursable only when used to distinguish cirrhosis from non-cirrhosis for members with hepatitis B, hepatitis C, MASLD/MASH, or alcoholic hepatitis, and only once every 180 days per member.

claims.summary: CA accounts for +$6.2M of the issue across four inpatient DRGs, led by bowel procedures at +$2.3M and digestive disorders at +$2.2M. AR adds +$1.4M from the same authorization code distribution issue. IN adds +$1.2M, concentrated in Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC. No admission or paid-per-admit metrics support a clean utilization or unit-cost interpretation because this is a coding or mapping validation pattern.

pattern_title: DC authorized inpatient spend is distorted by facility classification and site-of-care mix
pattern_description: DC has a concentrated increase in authorized inpatient spend tied to facility buckets labeled Not Mapped and OTHER. The pattern is present across TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual, with both more admissions and higher paid per admission. This looks like a mix of real site-of-care pressure and facility classification drift, so classification cleanup and business action need to run together.

rows.facility_scope: Applies to UB-04 inpatient/outpatient facility claims; inpatient tracheostomy/ventilation stay charges are bundled.
rows.bundling_rule: Routine services and supplies bundle into facility charges; only facility-owned ventilator/CPAP management is separate.

individual_policies.evidence: The policy does not name this DRG, but it contains directly relevant inpatient facility rules for tracheostomy and mechanical ventilation stays. Routine room-and-board, equipment, supply, nursing, respiratory, and tracheostomy-care charges are bundled into the inpatient facility payment. Management of a facility-owned ventilator or CPAP may be considered separately reimbursable for one unit per day, while related setup, checks, circuit changes, respiratory assessment, tracheostomy supplies/care, and similar ancillary components are not separately reimbursable.

pairing_conditions: critical care room other than recovery room
state_specific_rules: Hawaii: inpatient waitlist services and coordination of benefits billed with occurrence codes 74-76
District of Columbia: no current exemption listed; removed from exceptions in policy history on 3/1/2026

claims.summary: DC TANF Standard with facility Not Mapped drove +$4.5M from 92 more admissions and about +$31.2K paid per admit. DC TANF Standard with facility OTHER added +$1.3M with 57 more admissions and about +$1.9K paid per admit. DC ABD Non Dual with facility Not Mapped added +$0.6M with 16 more admissions and about +$37.7K paid per admit.

pattern_title: CA acute hospital admissions are rising with higher paid per admit in authorized Medicaid products
pattern_description: CA shows the largest clean operational growth pattern after validation issues are set aside. Authorized acute hospital spend is rising in TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual because admissions are up and paid per admit is also increasing. The pressure is concentrated in digestive, bowel, liver, obesity, and nerve disorder admissions rather than a broad all-category trend.

individual_policies.evidence: Off-topic for DRG reimbursement; the policy only addresses ICD-10 principal/first-listed diagnosis sequencing and does not govern this DRG concept.

claims.summary: CA TANF Standard acute hospital drove +$5.6M across digestive, bowel, cirrhosis, obesity, and nerve disorder DRGs. The largest CA driver was digestive disorders at +$2.0M with 248 more admissions and about +$3.1K higher paid per admit. CA bowel procedures added +$1.7M with 60 more admissions and about +$14.2K higher paid per admit. CA ABD Non Dual acute hospital added +$0.6M with 74 more admissions and about +$3.3K higher paid per admit.

pattern_title: CA inpatient case mix is shifting toward digestive, liver, obesity, and neuropathy admissions
pattern_description: CA also has a distinct clinical story separate from the operational acute-hospital mix. Growth is concentrated in recurring digestive, liver, obesity, and neuropathy diagnoses, with some emerging small-volume cases layered on top. Much of the increase appears volume-led, but some diagnoses also show higher intensity or higher paid per admit.

claims.summary: CA clinical case-mix groups total +$5.3M across recurring and emerging diagnoses. Alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites added +$0.8M with 66 more admissions even as paid per admit fell slightly. Metabolic syndrome within obesity procedures added +$0.8M with 35 more admissions. Noninfective gastroenteritis and colitis added +$0.4M with 56 more admissions and about +$1.0K paid per admit.

pattern_title: NC spend is highly concentrated at DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC
pattern_description: NC growth is concentrated in one provider, DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC, across both operational and clinical signals. The pattern combines higher authorized admission volume in Not Mapped facility claims with a small number of very high-cost transplant-related cases. This is a concentrated provider economics story, but mapping issues need to be resolved so the true facility and payment picture is clear.

DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC TANF Standard Not Mapped utilization added +$1.6M from 20 more admissions despite lower paid per admit, showing volume-led growth. pattern_title: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases are creating discrete high-cost spikes
pattern_description: Several states show isolated catastrophic inpatient episodes rather than a recurring utilization trend. These include tracheostomy and prolonged ventilation, craniotomy, burns, ECMO-level care, transplant, trauma, and other severe cases with very high paid amounts on very small numbers of admissions. The right response is claim-level and clinical validation, not broad policy changes.

claims.summary: A single DC tracheostomy and prolonged mechanical ventilation case added +$1.3M on 1 admission. A DC craniotomy case added another +$0.7M on 1 admission. AR trauma, pneumonia, and GI obstruction cases contributed about +$1.0M across 10 admissions. Rare burn, ECMO, and transplant episodes across FL, NC, OH, and VA added about +$0.9M, led by two SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL cases totaling +$0.6M.

pattern_title: VA spend is concentrated at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL across volume and unit-cost signals
pattern_description: VA shows a concentrated provider story at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL. Most of the increase comes from additional admissions in Not Mapped facility claims, while a separate acute-hospital pocket shows unit-cost pressure even as admissions decline. This is a focused provider economics and attribution pattern rather than a broad VA-wide inpatient trend.

VA TANF Standard acute hospital added +$0.2M from 21 more admissions even though paid per admit fell slightly. A separate VA TANF Standard acute-hospital unit-cost increase added +$0.2M while admissions declined by 8, showing reimbursement pressure on top of volume shifts.

pattern_title: Smaller state and product pockets show emerging authorized inpatient pressure
pattern_description: Outside the largest state and provider concentrations, there is a set of smaller authorized inpatient pockets that are individually modest but together meaningful. These pockets are spread across acute hospital, children's, acute psych, and some Not Mapped facility claims. Most are low-baseline or low-volume, so they should be managed as a targeted exception list rather than as an enterprise trend.

individual_policies.evidence: This policy limits inpatient DRG reimbursement when a health care-acquired condition is present. HCAC-related charges and days are removed from DRG calculation if identified through POA reporting.

AR LTSS Non Dual added +$0.5M in CHILDRENS and another +$0.3M across Not Mapped and ACUTE PSYCH settings.
